project.title: Many-body NHSE has a structural mother framework but no sector-independent invariant
project.hidden_assumption: A single sector-independent topological invariant should classify all many-body NHSE behavior.

contradiction.proposition_A: A unified description of non-Hermitian many-body skin effect exists.
contradiction.proposition_B: Sector and density dependence prevent a single invariant from classifying NHSE in all sectors.
contradiction.why_not_both: If unity is interpreted as one scalar invariant, sector dependence kills it; if unity is structural, a Stinespring mother framework can still organize the problem.
contradiction.resolution: The surviving object is a three-layer map: structural Stinespring framework, density-resolved diagnostics, and boundary caveats. The original sector-independent invariant claim fails.

lessons.lesson: A unifying structure and a unifying invariant are different claims; killing the latter does not kill the former.
Formal Lindblad operators should not be promoted to experimentally solved mechanisms without a physical realization path.
When a diagnostic is sector-resolved, its sector label is part of the observable definition.
